name: Meteora
title: Holidays in Meteora
intro: Monasteries perched on top of giant sandstone pillars rising from the plains of central Greece, a truly otherworldly sight. Here's what Meteora is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A monastery on top of a sheer rock pillar at Meteora
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April, May, September and October are best for walking between monasteries. July and August are very hot. Winter is cold and misty, which can look magical. Each monastery closes one day a week, so check before you go.

things.name: Great Meteoron
things.blurb: The largest monastery, with a museum and a frescoed church.

things.name: Varlaam
things.blurb: A monastery with an old rope-and-net lift still on show.

things.name: Roussanou
things.blurb: A nunnery reached by a bridge, on a narrow pillar.

things.name: Sunset viewpoint
things.blurb: Watch the sun set over the rocks from the viewpoints by the road.

things.name: Hiking trails
things.blurb: Old paths climb between the monasteries from Kastraki.

things.name: Rock climbing
things.blurb: Climbing routes for beginners and experts on the pillars.

faqs.question: Is Meteora worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of the most spectacular sights in Greece, a UNESCO site of monasteries on top of rock towers.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Meteora?
faqs.answer: One or two days covers the monasteries and a sunset. Stay a night in Kalambaka or Kastraki.

faqs.question: How do you get to Meteora?
faqs.answer: Fly to Thessaloniki or Athens, then take the train to Kalambaka, about 3 to 4 hours, or drive.

faqs.question: What should you wear to visit Meteora?
faqs.answer: Cover shoulders and knees. Women should wear skirts, which are usually lent at the entrances.
